label: text
text: HIS LORDSHIP'S THREAT

label: text
text:
FURTHER ATHERLEY CASE
EVIDENCE.

label: text
text: There was a dramatic interruption as this morning's hearing of Criminal Sessions proceedings against Mr. James Edward Atherley drew to its conclusion.

label: text
text: The compradore of Getz Bros. Co. (of the Orient). Ltd, was giving evidence with regard to the charges of fraudulent conversion against Mr. Atherley, the former manager, when he caught the eye of someone in the court and appeared to hesitate.

label: text
text: "My Lord," said Mr. Zeitlyn (instructed for prisoner by Messrs. Hall and Hind), "I saw that gentleman sitting next to the auditor. I don't know who he is, distinctly shake his head at the witness."

label: text
text: Mr. F. C. Jenkins (Instructed by Messrs. Wilkinson and Grist for the Attorney-General): It was very wrong of him to do so, if he actually did, but I can't say I noticed it. He is an interpreter in the employ of Messrs. Wilkinson and Grist.

label: text
text: His Lordship: Did the jury notice anything.

label: text
text: Mr. Silva (foreman) replied that they had noticed the man in question shake his head.

label: text
text: His Lordship (addressing the man in question): Get out of court. If I see anything of that kind again I will send you to prison for gross contempt of court.

label: text
text: The interpreter stopped on his way out to talk to a solicitor.

label: text
text: "Get out of court at once, sir," said His Lordship.

label: text
text: The compradore who was giving evidence at the time gave a different answer to the question asked him than he had done previously.

label: text
text: His Lordship drew his attention to this and asked him if this had anything to do with the other interpreter's signal.

label: text
text: The witness replied to the question of advances made to Mr. Atherley, that whatever bill of Mr. Atherley's he (the compradore) paid which Mr. Atherley said was not a personal account he looked to the Company to payment for.

label: text
text: Cross-examined by Mr. Zeitlyn, the compradore admitted making large loans to Mr. Atherley for his personal needs. These included rent of house, personal effects and clothes, drink, food, ferry ticket, hire of boys, services to house, etc.

label: text
text: Mr. Zeitlyn put it to witness that all the money transactions passing between him and Mr. Atherley throughout the whole period of the latter's duty as manager were transactions in which money was advanced for his personal use and personal security and were not to do with business.

label: text
text: This the witness denied and the question of an advance to Mr. Atherley of $1,500 for his wife's passage home then came under review. Witness admitted lending Mr. Atherley this money.

label: text
text: “Mr. Atherley told me that when I collected the money I was not to pay into the Bank because he wanted it for his wife's passage,” said the witness.

label: text
text: Mr. Zeitlyn: I put it to you that that is false. Do you think that his wife is a member of the Company?

label: text
text: Witness: Mr. Atherley was manager and when he wanted money I was bound by my agreement to pay him.

label: text
text: Mr. Zeitlyn: What clause of the agreement:

label: text
text: Witness quoted the part under which he could be called upon at any moment to account for and deliver company moneys.

label: text
text: Mr. Zeitlyn: Do you suggest that this is instruction to you to pay for the manager's baby's milk or his own champagne?

label: text
text: Witness maintained that he had no option but to pay money to the manager when he asked for

label: paragraph_title
text: 3ETTER HOPES.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOTEL CO'S LATEST ACTIVITIES.

label: text
text: A.B. BATCHELOR'S DEATH.

label: text
text: "Better than hoped for at first" is the opinion regarding the resumption of full activities at the Hongkong Hotel after the fire on New Year Day.

label: text
text: It is learned that steps will be taken to retrieve a part of the first floor of the main wing for use with the new building. A "China Mail" reporter was informed that a wall is likely to be erected shutting off the part considered dangerous. This course will mean the addition of more space in the hotel for public use.

label: text
text: Meanwhile Messrs. Palmer and Turner have still to decide more important questions.

label: text
text: It is also understood that the scaffolding erected around the damaged part will serve to remove, where possible, dangers, but demolishing work may not start for some days.

label: text
text: The Hotel management have written to Vice-Admiral Sir E. Alexander Sinclair asking for guidance as to giving tangible recognition of the service of A.B. Batchelor who was killed while assisting, as a volunteer, in fighting the fire. A reply is awaited.

label: paragraph_title
text: ASYLUM CASE

label: paragraph_title
text:
ALLEGED CONSPIRACY
CHARGES

label: text
text: Further evidence was taken at the Central Magistracy this morning in the case against two Chinese (one being a ward boy) charged with conspiring together to obtain the release of one Lee Ah-Lei, a patient at the Government Lunatic Asylum, together with his belongings, with intent to defraud.

label: text
text: At the previous hearing it was stated in evidence by Mr. James M. May, and award master that the first defendant, who claimed to be a broker of the patient, failed to give satisfactory answers to questions as to the patient's name and the date of his admittance. The police were then notified and took the men into custody.

label: text
text: Mr. M. W. Lo appeared for the first defendant this morning, when the case was again adjourned until Wednesday after the evidence of an office boy and another witness who was with the first defendant when the visit to the Asylum was made.

text: NEWS FOR PUBLIC.

label: paragraph_title
text: PEACE DELEGATES TO REPORT.

label: text
text: The Hon. Sir Shou-son Chow and the Hon. Mr. R. H. Kotewall have convened a meeting for this afternoon at the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, when the merchant delegates who have just returned from Canton will disclose their report.

label: text
text: An announcement appears in the vernacular papers asking the Chinese mercantile public to attend to hear what negotiations were conducted towards settlement of the strike.

text: URGES SUPPORT FOR TUAN CHI-JUI

label: text
text: General Ferry U-Shang has issued a circular telegram stating that he is given up public life and going abrush and urging the

label: text
text: military party to support Tuan Chi-jui in working for the settlement of the country.

label: text
text: Chief Executive (Tuan Chi jui) has sent General Liu Chi-lung to Kalgan, to consult with Feng Yu-hsiang about the advisability of Tuan retiring on January 15.

label: text
text: The spokesman of the Kuominchun (People's Army) states that Feng Yu-hsiang insists on retiring from public life. The statement is made that another circular telegram to that effect will be issued very shortly.

label: text
text: It is reported that Tu Hsi-kwai, who is under the patronage of Sun Chuan-fang, has telegraphed his refusal of the portfolio of Minister of the Navy.

label: paragraph_title
text: SUNDAY CINEMAS.

label: text
text: GOVERNMENT RESTRICTIONS WITH DRAWN.

label: text
text: WEEK DAY HOURS?

label: text
text: The “China Mall” understands officially that the restrictions hitherto obtaining in respect of Sunday cinema hours of opening have been withdrawn and that the Government has now no objection to the week day hours of opening applying to Sunday also.

label: text
text: A state of affairs thus ends as to the desirability of which public opinion was divided, although the general body of it (judging from very considerable correspondence in the "China Mail" last year) was, in favour of allowing such facilities. The "dullness" of a certain wet Sunday was used as an illustration by those favouring the removal of the restrictions.

label: text
text: The first sign of the Government's change of opinion was the concession made on Sunday, December 27, when week-day hours were allowed as it was holiday time. The appreciation of the change, voiced through the "China Mail," no doubt influenced the Government in coming to their decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: TRAFFIC OFFENCES.

label: text
text: THIS MORNING'S CASES

label: text
text: A SEQUEL TO A CHASE

label: text
text: At the Kowloon Magistracy this morning, Major Stanford was cautioned for leaving his motor car outside "Rogate" unattended on December 18.

label: text
text: Resulting from a complaint made by Mrs. W. W. Hirst, who was a passenger in a motor bus, the driver was charged with carrying five passengers in excess of the number allowed. A fine of $10 was imposed.

label: text
text: Mr John Manners was thanked by the Magistrate (Mr. E. W. Hamilton) after he had given evidence against a Chinese motor driver charged with reckless driving and on two other counts of having no lights. Witness said that his driver had to swerve to a side on the Castle Peak Road when the defendant's car came from the opposite direction travelling on the wrong side of the road at about 25 to 30 miles an hour. He gave chase and overtook the defendant's car, which had no rear light and only one front light. Fines of $50 and $10 were imposed on the first and third charges.

label: text
text: At the Central Magistracy this morning, Mr. G. H. Wilson was fined $5 for causing an obstruction by leaving his car in Pedder Street near the Hongkong Hotel.

label: paragraph_title
text: A GOOD REASON.

label: text
text:
WHY DEFENDANT WAS
ARSENT

label: text
text: HIS CHILDREN STOLEN.

label: text
text: The kidnapping of his two children was held to be quite sufficient reason for a defendant's non-appearance in court this morning.

label: text
text: A Chinese should have appeared in answer to a summons respecting money borrowing; but Mr. C. A. S. Russ handed in a letter received from the elders of the defendant's native village.

label: text
text: This letter concerned the whereabouts of the defendant's little boy and girl who lived up country and had been kidnapped for the purpose of holding them to ransom. The village elders had obtained knowledge of the whereabouts of the kidnappers and kidnapped and had written to the father telling him he must leave at once and instruct them.

label: text
text: The delay would probably be in the neighbourhood of three weeks said Mr. Russ and an adjournment for that period was granted.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOTEL FIRE.

label: text
text: CONFUSION CAUSED IN TOKYO.

label: text
text: TOURISTS INCONVENIENCED.

label: text
text: The “Nichi Nichi,” in a special report, states that fire destroyed the Nikko Hotel last night, causing confusion, as it was crowded with tourists from the liner “Belgenland”.

label: text
text: There were no casualties, but the loss is estimated at half a million yen.

label: paragraph_title
text: MUKDEN MENACE.

label: text
text: CHANG'S REGNET TO THE JAPANESE

label: text
text: REINFORCEMENTS, RECALLED:

label: text
text: London, January 5.

label: text
text: The War Department announces that the remaining reinforcements which were sent to Manchuria last month are withdrawing on Thursday and Friday and returning to Japan. It also announces that General Chang and General Son have sent messages to the Kwantung and Japanese authorities regretting that the recent disturbances threatened Japanese lives and property.

label: paragraph_title
text: KUO'S DOWNFALL

label: text
text: OFFICIALS STILL IN REFUGE.

label: text
text:
Foreign Office advises from Mukden state that eight of Kuo Burg-lin's civil officials are still taking refuge in the Japanese Consulate at Heinminfu.
Marshall Chang Tso-lin insists that they be turned over to him.
It is understood that the Japanese Government has instructed Consuls and railway guards that the refugees must be protected at all costs, thus creating a somewhat delicate situation via a vis Chang.
It is expected that extra guards will be sent from Mukden to Heimunfu for the purpose of escorting the refugees to the Mukden Consulate.
Chang Tso-lin's troops are said to be watching the Consulate at Heinminfu to prevent the escape of the refugees.
